messages:
sasha: quick RFC follow-up — i've been sketching a lightweight 'idle-set consolidation' approach where we only run compaction on a device when its active request queue goes to zero for > 150ms. aim is to avoid introducing tail latency from background compaction cycles during steady traffic. thoughts?
kevin: sounds promising. main thing i worry about is degenerating fragmentation if we wait too long. have we measured fragmentation growth curve?
maria: +1 to kev. if the fragmentation metric has long tails we might need a secondary trigger (eg: fragmentation > 25% or free contiguous < x). otherwise consolidation only on idle could be insufficient for long-lived hosts.
oliver: another trade: doing compaction only on idle reduces interference but increases frequency of big compactions when they do happen (more pages to move). need to cap max work per cycle and amortize.
sasha: agreed — proposed knobs in proto config:
```
compact:
  idle_threshold_ms: 150
  max_pages_per_cycle: 128
  backoff_ms: 250
  fragmentation_trigger_pct: 22
```
kevin: i like max_pages_per_cycle. also add a small randomized jitter to start times to avoid thundering herd across GPUs after a global lull.
janet: consider NUMA and PCIe impact — moving many pages off a big model checkpoint can saturate PCIe and mess SLOs for other tenants on same host. maybe honor a global bandwidth budget when deciding how many pages to migrate.
maria: +1. we can expose a host-level token-bucket: compaction_bytes_per_sec. infra-bot: host token-bucket updated: current_limit=200MB/s.
kevin: implementation question: do we keep a per-alloc 'fragmentation score' (cheap sample) or a rolling histogram of free-run lengths? histos give better decisions but heavier.
noliver: what if we maintain a coarse freelist-bucket histogram (powers-of-two bucket for run lengths) — light to update and gives good approx for largest-free-run. update cost = O(1) on free/alloc.
sasha: that seems sweet. also thinking about integrating resident-set feedback: if page-faults or KV-cache misses spike, prefer immediate lightweight compaction of affected arenas.
maria: useful: a small probe API for ops to request 'soft-compaction' on an arena: returns immediately if we are > idle_threshold, else enqueue and rate-limit. that lets higher layers hint critical fragments.
kevin: can we do 'copy-on-demand' instead of full-copy compaction? eg: mark cold pages and only relocate when next allocate needs contiguous run — this is lazy compaction, cheaper but can delay large contiguous allocations.
janet: lazy approach OK for some workloads but we should expose a deterministic fast-path for pinned ranges (e.g., parameters pinned for inference) so they never get fragmented/moved unexpectedly. pinned ranges should be skipped by background compaction.
sasha: agreed, pinned semantics: background compaction skips pinned; admin API can force-relocate pinned with explicit permission.
oliver: metrics we should add to console: compaction_cycles, pages_moved, average_cycle_duration_ms, compaction_bytes_throttled, fragmentation_pct_by_arena. these help tune knobs.
maria: and trace spans for compaction phases (scan, move, remap) — helps debug stop-the-world pauses.
sasha: perf checklist before we roll RFC: microbench alloc/free churn + long-running steady traffic to see fragmentation curve; end-to-end p99 on steady tail when compaction enabled; PCIe bandwidth sampling when compaction runs. i'll put a quick perf plan in the RFC PR.
kevin: one more nit — add simple safety: if compaction_cycle_time > panic_threshold_ms (eg 2s) abort and backoff. we don't want runaway migrations.
sasha: good call. i'll add abort/backoff.
janet: fine by me. if infra-bot can enforce host-level bandwidth and we expose metrics, we should be in a good place.
infra-bot: scheduled perf job: perf/compaction-idleset/200700/queued. ETA 48h.
sasha: thanks all — i’ll update RFC with the config schema and the freelist-histogram approach. will tag you for review.
